sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6: Quantum Electrodynamics
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; inspected §§6.1, 6.1.1, 6.2.1–6.2.2, 6.3.1, and the introductory scope of §6.4.

contents.name: §6.1 Maxwell’s Equations: field strength definition and source-free variational convention
contents.support: The item fixes its own metric and SI-natural normalization and states the local field-strength convention.

contents.name: §6.1.1 Gauge Symmetry: potential shifts and invariant field strength
contents.support: The item verifies the normalized gauge transformation and the invariance of f=da by commuting derivatives.

contents.name: §6.1.1 Gauge Symmetry: local phase and covariant derivative
contents.support: The local proof checks the matter phase and D_a covariance in the stated charge sign convention.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Coulomb Gauge: transverse modes and two polarization directions
contents.support: The local projection proof establishes the rank-two transverse fibers without choosing polarization vectors globally.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Coulomb Gauge: projected potential and equal-time commutator
contents.support: The item derives the smeared operator, its finite-particle domain and the transverse projector commutator.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Coulomb Gauge: Fourier kernel of the transverse projector
contents.support: The A-page lemma derives the Newtonian off-diagonal kernel from an Abel-regularized Fourier multiplier with complete local justification.

contents.name: §6.2.1 Coulomb Gauge: off-diagonal potential kernel
contents.support: The example computes a nonzero off-origin derivative of the Newtonian kernel.

contents.name: §6.2.2 Lorentz Gauge: subsidiary condition and null quotient
contents.support: The item proves the subsidiary space radical and its isometry to the positive transverse space.

contents.name: §6.2.2 Lorentz Gauge: negative auxiliary directions
contents.support: The counterexample exhibits a square-integrable negative-form vector outside the subsidiary space.

contents.name: §6.2.2 Lorentz Gauge: photon covariance
contents.support: The item verifies invariant cone measure, the quotient representation and the Fock future-cone spectrum.

contents.name: §6.3 Coupling to Matter and §6.3.1 Coupling to Fermions
contents.support: The local conditional proof derives the commuting-spinor variation, gauge covariance, Hamiltonian signs and current conservation.

contents.name: §6.3.1 Coupling to Fermions: first-order canonical data
contents.support: The finite proof computes primary constraints, the invertible constraint matrix and the reduced bracket.

contents.name: §6.4 QED: perturbative scattering and Feynman-rule development
contents.support: The later scattering and perturbative coefficient material belongs to subsequent QFT pages and is outside this charged-gauge-data pair.
contents.reason: The later scattering and perturbative coefficient material belongs to subsequent QFT pages and is outside this charged-gauge-data pair.

sources.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft
sources.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; inspected §§54–58. Srednicki uses different metric, index and charge conventions; this batch translates them explicitly.

contents.name: §54 Maxwell’s Equations
contents.support: The source defines the potential and field strength; the local item independently fixes lower-potential and SI-natural signs.

contents.name: §55 Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge
contents.support: The local bounded projection construction replaces a pointwise polarization basis.

contents.name: §55 Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge: canonical transverse commutator
contents.support: The local CCR calculation proves the same projector kernel on finite-particle vectors.

contents.name: §55 Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge: inverse Laplacian kernel
contents.support: The local proof verifies the inverse Fourier transform and the off-origin Newtonian derivative used to interpret the projector.

contents.name: §55 Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge: Poisson and Coulomb kernel
contents.support: The local Fourier regularization identifies the off-origin Newtonian derivative and limits the nonlocality claim to the potential.

contents.name: §56 LSZ Reduction for Photons
contents.support: Asymptotic scattering reduction is not required for the free one-particle space or local smeared observables authored in this pair.
contents.reason: Asymptotic scattering reduction is not required for the free one-particle space or local smeared observables authored in this pair.

contents.name: §57 The Path Integral for Photons
contents.support: The formal functional-integral treatment is outside this pair; no path-integral measure or continuum construction is asserted here.
contents.reason: The formal functional-integral treatment is outside this pair; no path-integral measure or continuum construction is asserted here.

contents.name: §58 Spinor Electrodynamics: local gauge transformation and covariant derivative
contents.support: The local proof verifies the same covariance and current identities after translating the author’s sign and metric conventions.

contents.name: §58 Spinor Electrodynamics: charged Dirac kinetic term
contents.support: The finite commuting-mode reduction is proved directly and explicitly kept distinct from CAR quantization.

sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2
sources.locator: Author-hosted complete chapter-2 PDF; inspected Theorem 2.28 and its proof on pp.134–135.

contents.name: Theorem 2.28: no nowhere-zero tangent vector field on an even sphere
contents.support: The local proof specializes the theorem to S² after mapping a hypothetical global polarization frame to a unit tangent field.

sources.title: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition, version 4.01
sources.locator: Official complete brochure; §2.2 defining constants and §2.3.1 ampere, including the current experimentally determined status of μ0.

contents.name: §2.2 Defining Constants: exact c and h
contents.support: The conventions retain c and h symbolically and use no empirical numerical substitution.

contents.name: §2.3.1 Ampere: μ0 is experimentally determined in the current SI
contents.support: The definition deliberately leaves μ0 symbolic and adopts no measured value or precision.
